title: Wildcard-Import Ambiguity (The Orphan rule collide)
pattern: Downstream crates use wildcard imports (`use crate::*`), and an upstream crate introduces a new public trait or method with a name that collides with a downstream trait implemented for the same type.
why_bad: It causes silent compilation breakages on minor upstream updates. Even though both traits are technically distinct, the downstream compiler cannot resolve the ambiguous method name on `Unit.foo()`, halting developer builds unexpectedly.
detection: The combination of wildcard imports (`*`) in client modules combined with the upstream introduction of traits containing common method names (like `run`, `init`, or `save`).
counterexample: Explicit imports or strict module qualification paths where the namespace is unambiguously declared.
fix: Avoid exporting general wildcard preludes. Instruct library consumers to use explicit imports or wrap foreign types using the newtype pattern to isolate method resolution.
source: Jon Gjengset, *Rust for Rustaceans* (2021), Chapter 4 ("Coherence and the Orphan Rule"), pp. 87-88, 93-94.
